stories.normalized_subject: nvidia reportedly asks global cloud partners to keep 51% of services outside china
stories.event_summary: The Financial Times reports that Nvidia has told data-centre partners worldwide to direct at least 51% of their cloud services to customers outside China. The instruction was reportedly delivered verbally by sales and regional teams, applies to future contracts and leaves existing leases untouched. The FT cites five people familiar with the policy; it has not published a written Nvidia rule. Nvidia’s public response defended the role of US-built data centres and said longstanding US policy encourages American infrastructure to win business worldwide. That statement did not confirm the reported 51% requirement. If enforced, the rule could make overseas GPU leasing harder for Chinese model developers and change the economics of cloud operators in Southeast Asia and other regional hubs.

stories.normalized_subject: crowdstrike is buying agent observability and ai red-team tools — and adding a kill switch

The Wall Street Journal reports a combined price of $495m, mostly cash; CrowdStrike’s official announcements do not disclose the purchase price. Fiddler is intended to add pre-deployment evaluation, traceability of decisions and tool calls, and production monitoring. CrowdStrike says it plans to support OpenTelemetry and frameworks including LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Strands and Google ADK. Dreadnode is designed to run more than 100 attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection and multi-turn agent attacks, against models, applications and MCP servers. Separately, CrowdStrike announced an AI kill switch and an AI Gateway in Falcon Guardian. The gateway is available now; endpoint termination is described as coming later. Acquired Fiddler and Dreadnode capabilities are planned for general availability in Q4 FY27, subject to closing and integration.
